DeveloperDocs.title: Build signals with the SDK, run execution with the local executor
DeveloperDocs.description: A practical guide for using the published Quant Signal SDK and the Marcus Local Executor Client without mixing their responsibilities.

overview.sdkDescription: The Python package for modeling, validating, backtesting, uploading, and publishing Marcus trading signals.
overview.executorDescription: The trader-side runtime that connects to the dispatcher, receives signals, and executes orders through an exchange account.
overview.flowDescription: Developers publish signed signals. Traders run the executor with their own exchange credentials and execution mode.

sdk.title: Quant Signal SDK
sdk.description: Install the published package from PyPI, build SignalPayload objects, send them through QuantSignalClient, and use quant-sdk for local backtests and uploads.

capabilities.models: Pydantic signal models and enums for actions, market type, order type, status, and execution policies.
capabilities.strategy: BaseStrategy and runtime interfaces keep strategy logic separate from transport and signing.
capabilities.backtest: PortfolioBacktestRunner replays OHLCV data locally without placing exchange orders.
capabilities.upload: Backtest upload can publish historical results to the Marcus backend as a batch report.
capabilities.sync: Dry-run sync helpers persist paper-trading state separately from historical backtests.
capabilities.telemetry: TelemetryClient is reserved for operational metrics such as CPU, latency, and heartbeat-style signals.

executor.title: Marcus Local Executor Client
executor.description: Run the executor as a local or Dockerized runtime. It maintains WebSocket connectivity, validates signal frames, records local SQLite state, and routes orders through CCXT in dry-run or live mode.

requirements.wsUrl: SYSTEM_WS_URL points to the Marcus executor WebSocket endpoint for the deployment you are using.
requirements.wsToken: SYSTEM_WS_TOKEN authenticates the executor WebSocket handshake.
requirements.botId: BOT_ID binds the runtime to the provisioned Marcus bot.
requirements.exchange: Exchange credentials stay on the trader side and are required for live mode.
requirements.amount: DEFAULT_ORDER_AMOUNT provides the fallback order amount when a signal does not include one.
requirements.mode: EXECUTION_MODE must be dry-run for safe logging or live for real exchange orders.

boundaries.title: Keep SDK and executor responsibilities separate
boundaries.description: This distinction is important for security, product truthfulness, and support.

notes.sdkNoExchange: The SDK does not place real exchange orders. It creates, validates, signs, backtests, uploads, and publishes signals.
notes.executorRuntime: The executor is the runtime that receives accepted signals and executes them in dry-run or live mode through the trader exchange account.
notes.deploymentConfig: Backend and WebSocket URLs are deployment configuration. They should not be treated as hard-coded product branding.

next.label: Next step
